openQuestions: The full unit suite was run once before the last fix: 1 file failed (engine-states.test.ts, 4 tests pinning a stored Codex filing engine), 462 passed. Those assertions and their ctx fixtures were changed from 'codex' to 'claude' (lines 31 onward; the two engineStates tests are untouched) and the file passes; the whole suite was not re-run after that edit.

Deviates from the design on purpose, per the previous findings: the first line is not awaited before runComet. It is shown the moment haiku answers (within 1.5 s) unless the answer has produced a token; the main prompt gets the exact line if it was already shown when the prompt is built, otherwise a generic 'a first line may already be on screen, do not restate the job' sentence.

Because the line is shown as soon as it arrives, a very fast haiku answer could be saved as a progress turn before the user's turn is appended (ipc.ts handleChatSend) and can precede an error reply. Not covered by a test.

No voice warm-up remains anywhere (boot warm in index.ts and per-turn warm in ipc.ts removed). The first eligible turn after launch or after the voice's idle close starts the haiku runtime cold and will usually miss the 1.5 s budget; later turns use the warm voice.

One-line questions up to 40 characters and greeting/thanks openers are skipped locally without a model call; a short job phrased as a question (e.g. 'Can you draft the Q3 report?') therefore gets no haiku line.

Claude's command sandbox is on by default on macOS (ENGRAM_CLAUDE_SANDBOX=0 turns it off). Its real confinement (no network, private folder unreadable, writes only in the task folder, failIfUnavailable) was not exercised: the SDK types were not present in node_modules and the option names come from the design's reading of @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.272. If the sandbox cannot start on a Mac, native Claude turns fail visibly rather than run unsandboxed. Needs a live check on a signed-in Mac.

Tier log purposes: 'work', 'first-line', 'title', 'memory' (wrapped at the rememberTurn call in ipc.ts), and 'librarian' for any background run() with no named purpose or the gate's default 'memory-maintenance'. Other named contexts log their own purpose (skill-distillation, brief-speech, habit-drafts, work-map-labels).
session-watch.ts and first-filing run through the same un-named path and therefore log as 'librarian'.
